hypothesis: Across continental and near-continental islands, the fraction of an island's terrestrial mammal species that also occur on the neighbouring mainland decreases with the maximum depth of the sea channel separating them, and this relationship holds after controlling for the width of the channel; islands whose channel is shallower than the Pleistocene low stand (about 120 m) share more species than islands whose channel is deeper.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered: for each of 28 fixed islands, (i) the terrestrial mammal species set (GBIF Mammalia occurrences with >= 3 records inside the island box, minus bats, cetaceans, sirenians, pinnipeds and 12 domestic or commensal genera), (ii) the same for a fixed neighbouring-mainland box, (iii) channel depth = greatest water depth (GEBCO 2020 via the OpenTopoData API, 100 points) along a fixed straight transect between the nearest island and mainland shores, and (iv) channel width = transect length. f = |island ∩ mainland| / |island|. SUPPORTS if all of: Spearman rho(f, log depth) < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; partial Spearman of f on log depth controlling log width < 0 with one-sided p < 0.05; mean f of islands with depth <= 120 m exceeds mean f of islands with depth > 120 m.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered: REFUTES if Spearman rho(f, log depth) >= 0 or if mean f of shallow (<= 120 m) islands is <= mean f of deep (> 120 m) islands. Any other outcome is MIXED. Islands with fewer than 5 qualifying species are dropped; with fewer than 12 islands remaining the result is inconclusive (underpowered). If the bathymetry API is unreachable the result is inconclusive (data-unavailable).
interpretation: 'Terrestrial mammals' excludes bats (Darwin treats them separately), marine mammals and species carried by humans (domestic stock, commensal rodents, Homo); other introductions remain in GBIF and bias against the claim by making deep-water islands look similar to the mainland. 'Depth of sea' is the present maximum depth along a straight line between the nearest shores; Darwin's reasoning is about former land connections, so the 120 m Pleistocene low-stand depth is the pre-registered dividing line, and present depth is an imperfect stand-in for past connection (caveat). 'Same or allied species' is measured at the species level only (shared species fraction); genus-level affinity is recorded as a secondary descriptive measure. For Wallacean islands (Sulawesi, Lombok) the Sunda-shelf islands Borneo and Bali serve as the 'mainland', and for Hokkaido and Ireland the larger neighbouring islands (Honshu, Great Britain) do, as Darwin himself discusses Britain and its islands; this is noted.
